pull.title: Build expectrail trust-check and put the receipt check in the wheel
pull.body:
Part of #255

## What was built

`expectrail trust-check`, which was a planned command that said "not built yet (#255)".
- It runs the receipt check from `expectrail.receipt`: the same `check_receipt` and the same report as `python3 -m expectrail.receipt trust-check`.
- Exit 0 is clearance, 1 is no clearance, 5 is "nothing was checked". That covers a receipt or trust store that cannot be read (missing, not JSON, not UTF-8, not canonical) and a command line that cannot be read. Nothing goes to stdout then. The module command keeps 2 for that case.
- A file that is not UTF-8 gave a traceback from both commands. Both now say nothing was checked.
- `expectrail.receipt` is now in the wheel. It finds its schema through `resources.ROOT`.
- A new `trust` extra (`cryptography>=42`, `jsonschema>=4.20`). A verification still needs only the standard library. Without the extra, the command names the missing package and `pip install 'expectrail[trust]'`, checks nothing and exits 5.
- `docs/install.md`: `repair` is built, so it gets its own row, and `trust-check` gets its row and the extra.

## What was run, and its result

- The full suite on the branch merged with main at 9ba5c38: 3,896 tests, OK, 40 skipped.
- `tests.test_package` built the wheel and ran two tests on the installed copy:
  - With the standard library only, the command fails closed with exit 5.
  - With the host's `cryptography` and `jsonschema` on the path, a real signed receipt gets clearance (exit 0). With no policy given it gets no clearance (exit 1). The module and its schema load from the installed copy.
- Three mutations were each caught:
  - the schema path left beside the package;
  - every missing module reported as the extra;
  - `ValueError` not caught.
- CI: not read when this was written.

Guard: test change intended (#255)
`tests/test_doctor.py` asserted `cli.PLANNED == ["trust-check"]` and `tests/test_package.py` used `trust-check` as its example of a command that is not built. That command is now built, so `PLANNED` is empty. The first test asserts it is empty. The second is replaced by the two installed-copy tests above. The planned-command path keeps a test in `tests/test_trust_check_command.py`, which uses a made-up command.

## What is left

On #255:
- CI attestation (`id-token: write`, `attestations: write`). This is Sean's.
- Writing the receipt from the trusted job.
- A real CI receipt through `gh attestation verify` and `trust-check`.
- The trust store's distribution and rotation.
- A receipt row in the capability ledger.

## Anything only a person may do

Nothing for this pull request.

## Checklist

- [x] `python3 -m unittest discover -s tests -t .` passes on this branch (merged with main at 9ba5c38)
- [x] One file added under `docs/new-work/`: `2026-11-15-package-trust-check.md`
- [x] No `approval` added or changed, nothing under `game/platformer` or `game/unity-platformer` edited
- [x] No test deleted or skipped; two existing assertions changed, with the reason and the Guard line above
- [x] No schema changed

<!-- expectrail-gate:v0 -->
### Expectrail: accept

**All 2 checks pass after this change.** Accepted means this change passed these checks on these routes, not that the game is correct.

<details><summary>All 2 public checks</summary>

| Check | Route | Before | After | Comparison | Finding |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| player-stays-above-ground | combat | pass | pass | PRESERVED |  |
| player-stays-above-ground | smoke | pass | pass | PRESERVED |  |

</details>

**Declared as:** nothing declared: judged as a change that should break no check.

**Held-out routes:** not used on this run.

**Checks used:** 1 approved spec on 2 routes, from the base commit `ec4c1f55bd07`, so this change cannot edit them. spec player\-stays\-above\-ground: approved before content binding.

**Replays in the sandbox:** all 4, in bubblewrap 0.9.0: no network, the game's own files only \(required\).

**Judged on:** two observers on every check: the engine's record, and sam\-recorded \(sam\-3.1, recorded: clean, fall\-through\-bug, fall\-through\-repair, gate\-combat\) over the captured frames; a check passes only when both pass.

**Evidence:** the review page (`review/index.html`), the verdicts and findings.json are in the `expectrail-report` artifact of [run 43768383167](https://github.com/Expectrail/Expectrail/actions/runs/43768383167). The comparisons use the review's words: [how to read a review](https://github.com/Expectrail/Expectrail/blob/main/docs/review.md). [How this gate works and its limits](https://github.com/Expectrail/Expectrail/blob/main/docs/ci-gate.md).

<sub>Commit `6740d7e5cdca`. Expectrail 0.1.0 at `ec4c1f55bd07`. A finding id is the first 12 hex digits of sha256(spec, route, kind), so a failure keeps its id across pushes. The trusted job judged the saved replays.</sub>
